name: superpowers
description: An agentic skills framework & software development methodology that works.
one_liner: A rulebook that makes your AI coding assistant stop and plan properly, writing a spec and getting your sign-off before it builds anything, instead of charging ahead and making a mess.
buyer: An engineering lead at a small company who has let the team loose on AI coding assistants and is now worried about unreviewed, inconsistent code piling up.
business_use_cases: An engineering manager installs it across the team so every AI-assisted feature goes through a forced spec-and-plan step before code gets written, cutting down on rework.
A dev agency uses the structured spec-to-plan-to-build workflow as a repeatable process they can point clients to, making AI-assisted delivery feel less like a black box.
A solo founder with no engineering background uses the enforced methodology to keep an AI agent from quietly cutting corners while building their first product.

money_ideas.idea: Offer paid enterprise support, additional tooling, or managed spend controls for companies rolling it out at scale, as the project itself already advertises.
Run paid workshops teaching teams how to adopt the subagent-driven-development workflow effectively.

steal_this: It's a process framework for developers, not an end-customer product; the real move is adopting it on your own team and, if it works, offering to set it up for other small dev shops for a fee.
